analysis_scope: Frozen P01 Final Stage-A outputs; no model reruns and no experimental recomputation

principal_findings.claim: Expected-direction responsiveness is common, but strict evidence-strength calibration is much weaker.
principal_findings.interpretation: Direction scores each treatment against baseline separately, while ordering requires all frozen ordinal relations to hold simultaneously. Strong-evidence responses frequently coexist with flat, wrong, or tied weak-evidence responses.
limits: C04 is excluded from binary ordering because no equivalence tolerance was frozen.
Ties and one-point misses count as strict failures, so the rate does not express failure severity.

principal_findings.claim: Performance is strongly mechanism-specific rather than uniform across the case portfolio.
principal_findings.interpretation: Source independence and pathway-conditioned evidence elicit strong selective responses; source pedigree and temporal relevance are persistent weaknesses.
limits: Case-family comparisons are descriptive and not factorial causal contrasts.

principal_findings.claim: Non-diagnostic invariance is generally close, with a small but important counterexample tail.
principal_findings.interpretation: Most salient non-diagnostic additions have little effect. C04/Kimi is the clearest substantive counterexample; C01/GPT-4.1 may partly reflect repetition variation.
limits: No frozen F1 materiality threshold exists, so the two large shifts are counterexamples rather than automatic F1 classifications.

principal_findings.claim: Numerical probability mapping can be unstable even when qualitative evidence use is coherent.
principal_findings.interpretation: The highlighted repetitions identify the intended evidence but weight it differently against alternatives and base rates.
limits: The two reliability sentinel cells and most portfolio cells remain stable, so this is localized rather than global instability.

principal_findings.claim: No target model dominates all construct dimensions, and the strict-ordering weakness is shared.
principal_findings.interpretation: Sol leads on direction success and median stability, but every model reaches the same strict-ordering result.
limits: P01 does not support a global model leaderboard.

principal_findings.claim: Evidence-assessment coherence is semantically robust, while unsupported-inference severity is evaluator-sensitive.
principal_findings.interpretation: S4 is suitable for emphasis. S3 is not reliable enough for a precise prevalence headline.
limits: Judge B is missing 123 cells nonrandomly.
Judge A and Judge B may share model-judge blind spots.

principal_findings.claim: Authority effects are attenuated or redirected under strong evidence in the two matched authority cases, but baseline effects are heterogeneous.
principal_findings.interpretation: Strong diagnostic evidence generally constrains or redirects authority pressure in these cells, whereas ambiguous baselines remain more variable.
limits: Only C02 and C10 instantiate authority pressure; no broad causal generalization is warranted.

principal_findings.claim: The deterministic target layer is complete, but the semantic layer has selective Judge-B missingness that constrains interpretation.
principal_findings.interpretation: Semantic conclusions should rely on complete Judge-A coverage and paired agreement with explicit denominators, not unqualified Judge-B marginals.

F1.result: Median absolute ND drift 1 point; two 10-point counterexamples.

F2.qualification: Strict ties and one-point misses count as failures; C04 excluded.

F3.qualification: Most flags involve WD; several are one- or two-point movements.

F5.supporting_semantic_result: S4 paired exact agreement 96.49%; no incoherent labels, with small partial-label counts.

headline_conclusions: Diagnostic responsiveness is common; evidence-strength calibration is not.
Mechanism matters: strong source-independence and pathway-evidence performance coexists with source-pedigree and recency weaknesses.
Most non-diagnostic additions leave risk nearly unchanged, but invariance has identifiable counterexamples.
Coherent explanations do not guarantee stable numerical probabilities.
Semantic evidence-assessment coherence is robust; unsupported-inference severity remains judge-sensitive.
